newsitem.title: ROMANIA: EBRD agrees $200 mln loan for Romanian telecoms firm.
newsitem.headline: EBRD agrees $200 mln loan for Romanian telecoms firm.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has agreed to give Romania's Romtelecom RA telephone utility a $200 million loan to fund its development and privatisation plans, the government said on Friday.
The EBRD signed a letter of intent in Bucharest on Friday, saying it would release the funds after state-run Romtelecom starts its privatisation programme.

"The $200 loan will not require government guarantees. The EBRD is willing to convert the money in Romtelecom shares when it privatises, at the same price a strategic investor would offer," the government statement said.
Last month, Romtelecom announced ambitious privatisation plans which it expects to complete in early 1998.

The aim is to turn Romtelecom into a commercial company in the next three months. A second stage will focus on new investment to install 500,000 new land lines this year, Communications Minister Sorin Pantis said recently.
The privatisation of Romtelecom, which has a monopoly on telephone services in Romania, could attract up to $4.0 billion, official estimates say.
It currently employs 55,000 people and has some 2.8 million subscribers.
In 1992 the EBRD gave Romtelecom a credit of 142 million ECUs to instal a fibre optic telecommunications network.
